Hi @rubberyuzu,

You seem to have opened [4 separate draft pull requests](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pulls/rubberyuzu). Usually, we have people wait to open a pull request until the feature is ready, and once it is ready, they only open one.

Would you be willing to close some of these? Giving all the 672 watchers of these repositories updates on every PR can be a bit confusing.

Hi Domenic, thanks for pointing this out! I created the draft PRs just to generate HTML diff files so I didn't need most of them open, so I closed three of them and left this one open.
(If there's any good way to produce HTML diff when creating PRs in private repo, please let me know.)

You can create diffs using either the Git command line tools, or the GitHub web UI. For an example of the latter, see https://github.com/whatwg/html/compare/main...rubberyuzu:html:build-nrr-document (click on the "Files changed" tab).

Sorry @domenic, I was the one that suggested her to open a draft PR, to get the auto-generated HTML diff preview (not the source diff) to make it easier for reviewers of @rubberyuzu's PR in her own repos. Didn't realize that it's visible in the PR lists still and also updates all watchers :(

Is it ok to keep just 1 draft PR here for this purpose (if there's a way to make it not noisy to watchers)? If not probably we'll just go with uploading the generated HTML in @rubberyuzu's PRs manually instead. Sorry for the noise!
No worries! One draft PR seems fine.
Thanks for the review Domenic! I think I addressed all of your comments. PTAL again :)
Thanks! I think I addressed all the comments. PTAL again

Thanks for the comment!
Right, it makes sense that notRestoredReasons should not belong to DocumentState given its lifecycle. We can maybe keep the reasons in Document or DocumentState initially, and then move it to SessionHistory (or something else that remains after document destruction) when the document gets destroyed or when document gets restored. I think notRestoredReasons should belong to whatever realm/globals/Window NavigationTimingEntry belongs to.

As for your code example, `navigationTimingEntryFromChild.notRestoredReasons` will always be null because notRestoredReasons only gets attached to top-level main frame.

Please let me know what you think.

> As for your code example, navigationTimingEntryFromChild.notRestoredReasons will always be null because notRestoredReasons only gets attached to top-level main frame.

Ah, right, that makes this easier! OK then. Here is my suggested strategy.

Define a [struct](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#structs) called "not restored reasons". It has a src, id, name, URL, reasons, and children. Besides being a struct instead of an interface, its fields have the following differences:
- Its URL field should be a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)
- Its reasons is a [list](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#lists) of strings, instead of an observable array.
- Its children is a list of not restored reasons structs, instead of an observable array of `NotRestoredReasons` objects.

(You'll need to go back to defining the reasons and children items explicitly.) Some example struct definitions in the spec are https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#coop-enforcement-result and https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#source-snapshot-params .

Now basically convert all the work you've done to operate on this not restored reasons struct. It's fine to store that in document state (since it's realm-independent). You can build it in basically the same way.

Now we need to redefine the `NotRestoredReasons` interface. Update it to only have one private member: a not restored reasons. (I'm unsure on a good name for this member. Maybe "backing struct", or maybe just "not restored reasons". Up to you.) And then update all its non-ObservableArray getters to return the corresponding item from the backing struct. For the url getter, you'll need to have it serialize the URL.

To handle the observable array items, add a small wrapper algorithm, "create a `NotRestoredReasons` object", given a not restored reasons struct and a realm. This algorithm creates a new `NotRestoredReasons`, sets its backing struct, and then copies the reasons and children across into the `reasons` and `children` backing lists. For reasons, you can just [extend](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend) the backing list. For `children`, you'll need to loop and append, at each step recursively calling "create a `NotRestoredReasons` object" to convert from the not restored reasons struct to a `NotRestoredReasons` object.

OK, we're almost done. The final step is to be clear on how we'll specify `navigationTimingEntry.notRestoredReasons`. You'd define that `NavigationTimingEntry` objects have a notRestoredReasons private value, which starts null. Then update [create a navigation timing entry](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry) to fill it in using "create a `NotRestoredReasons` object" given the document's node navigable's active session history entry's document state's not restored reasons. Then, the getter steps for `notRestoredReasons` can return the notRestoredReasons private value.

All this ensures that we create the `NotRestoredReasons` object once per document, while the persistent not restored reasons structs can stick around in session history as necessary.

I hope this makes sense! I'm sorry we spotted this so late. Hopefully it's not too much of a pain to change.

Thanks Domenic for the suggestion! I have a question:

> then update all its non-ObservableArray getters to return the corresponding item from the backing struct

The new NotRestoredReasons interface only has a not restored reasons struct as its member right? Even so does it still define getters for not restored reasons' items (such as url and src)?
Please let me know if there is any existing example like this. 

Thanks in advance!

Yes, that's right. You would define them roughly like the following:

> The `src` getter steps are to return this's backing struct's src.
Thanks! Another small question: Can the dom-intro (note to developers) section stay there under the struct, or should it be removed?
That part should stay with the definition of the `NotRestoredReasons` interface.

I see. Does NotRestoredReasons interface have getters for src, id and name etc. even though it does not have them as a member? Also, backingStruct is a private member so we should not define getters for it?

> Does NotRestoredReasons interface have getters for src, id and name etc. even though it does not have them as a member?

Yes; because those are part of the IDL, you need to define getters for them.

> Also, backingStruct is a private member so we should not define getters for it?

Yes. It does not appear in the IDL, so it has no getter.
PTAL again, I think I included all the suggested changes.
Thanks for the review and sorry for the delay! PTAL again.
Thanks so much Domenic! I think I addressed all the points. PTAL again :)
Done, thanks!
I guess keeping ObservableArray and make it empty for cross-origin iframes is also an option.

Right, I noted that over in https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/1337. We could work on the spec + implementation work to make that possible, as an alternative.

But honestly, in this case, FrozenArray might be a better fit anyway. ObservableArray was mostly meant to be used when something could change over time. In practice, there's very little observable difference between an ObservableArray that never changes and disallows modifications, vs. a FrozenArray. The only observable difference for web developers is that `Object.isFrozen(nrr.reasons)` will return true. But that behavior does feel slightly more accurate, so it's a point in favor of FrozenArray.

Unfortunately the way to spec FrozenArray properties is different from how you spec ObservableArray ones. Here's what you'd do:

- Add "reasons array, a `FrozenArray<NotRestoredReasons` or null, initially null" and similarly for "children array", as internal fields of `NotRestoredReasons`. Those two would sit alongside "backing struct". (The spec has [one existing somewhat-similar example](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-datatransfer-types).)

- Add `reasons` and `children` getter steps, which return this's reasons/children array. (You don't get automatically-generated getter steps, for FrozenArray attributes.)

- In "create a NotRestoredReasons object", instead of setting `reasons` to null / extending `reasons`'s backing list / appending to `children`'s backing list, you would modify the "reasons array" or "children array".
  - For the null case, just set those internal fields to null.
  - For the non-null case, you need to call [create a frozen array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-create-frozen-array) given an appropriate Infra list. So e.g. "creating a frozen array given _backingStruct_'s reasons". And for children, first create an empty list, append the result of creating a NotRestoredReasons object (similar to what you're currently doing in step 4.1) to that list, then finally set the "children array" to the result of creating a frozen array from that list.
Hi @domenic , thanks for the advice. I started using FrozenArray in the draft. PTAL!

Thanks! PTAL again.

FYI: I'm adding WPTs to test all the reasons added in the spec. The tracking bug is [here](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1472637).
Thanks Domenic, now the build is complete. Can you please merge it? Thanks again!
@zcorpan, can you confirm Mozilla's support for the spec?
Our feedback hasn't been addressed.

@smaug---- can you comprehensively summarize that feedback? This is a long thread and some comments have been hidden. Is your only current objection your latest comment, that the non-normative description of the `fetch` blocking reason is hard for you to understand?

I think the main comments we have are about not exposing the reason for cross-origin iframes and then also the vagueness around worker-initiated things.

For cross-origin iframes, we still think this API shouldn't expose anything about the reason that they block the top-level page from going into the bfcache. Given that, we think the random selection is unnecessary complexity. In fact, I think that the API could be simplified even further by dropping `preventedBackForwardCache`. For the `reasons` array there would be 2 cases:

1. top-level or same-origin iframe:
- not blocked from BFCache: empty array
- blocked from BFCache for a reason that's in the spec: array contains one or more of the strings from the spec (`fetch`, `websocket`, …)
- blocked from BFCache but the browser doesn't expose the reason: array contains a special value (`unknown`, `masked`, …?). For the top-level pages this includes the case where a cross-origin iframe blocked the top-level page from going into the bfcache. It includes the case where the browser is blocking for internal reasons (memory limits, …). It probably also includes the cases where a browser blocks for a feature that's currently not in the spec.

2. cross-origin iframe:
- emtpy array

For worker-initiated things we would like to see as much vagueness as possible removed.

@smaug---- @petervanderbeken 

For cross-origin iframes, I'd like to echo what Fergal said in this comment: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9360#discussion_r1266356669

1. Revealing that cross-origin blocking has occurred is actionable and important for devs to be able to increase their hit rate.
2. Whether cross-origin iframes blocked can already be inferred by devs and random selection is giving no more information than that.
3. It would be confusing to have an empty array `[]` when actually blocking. 

As to worker-initiated fetch, Domenic commented that we could add "in the context of document (including any initiated by Workers whose owner set contains the single item document)" here:
https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9360#discussion_r1285506518
Let me know if you agree with this or not.

Thanks!

@petervanderbeken thank you.

@rubberyuzu 
> 3 It would be confusing to have an empty array [] when actually blocking.

I don't think that is their prooposal. It would have "internal" or some other reason that makes it hard to know for sure because it can occur in other circumstances.

I'm not convinced that that's a workable idea though. If `a.com` is determined to extract this bit of info from `b.com`, it can 

- Create a page with N `a.com` iframes
- Each iframe contains nothing but a `b.com` iframe
- I know that each of these can have no blocking reason of their own except possibly some "internal" reason because they use no APIs etc
- In Chrome, almost all internal reasons are either
  - unspecced reasons that prevent the page going into BFCache at all (although I would prefer to surface them as specific reasons, not jus bucket them as "internal")
  - the result of some unfortunate timing, e.g. an event arrived that could not be processed while in BFCache (perhaps it raced with the navigation or perhaps we have some sources of rare events that we haven't noticed and haven't disabled while in BFCache)
  - also, over time the number of occurrences of "internal" should reduce, ideally to close to zero
- If
  - `b.com` blocks BFCache, it presumably blocks it in all of those iframes. This means that all of the `a.com` iframes will show "internal" as a blocking reason.
  - `bcom` doesn't block BFCache then at most one of the `a.com` iframes will show "internal" as a blocking reason

I think N only needs to 2 and you could do this for multiple cross-oirigin frames per page.

That implies is that we either have to give no reason at all when a cross-origin iframe bloccks or go with the randomness to limit what can be discovered per navigation.

>     1. Revealing that cross-origin blocking has occurred is actionable and important for devs to be able to increase their hit rate.
>     2. Whether cross-origin iframes blocked can already be inferred by devs and random selection is giving no more information than that.

We're not arguing that it's not actionable. The question is how much you want to disclose this cross-origin. We think that devtools is for example one place where developers should be able to get more information for cross-origin iframes, but this specific API isn't.
There are ways to gather the blocking status of cross-origin iframes currently, but they are pretty convoluted if there are multiple iframes involved. The random selection is a pretty weird API, and we'd rather not give a reason at all.

>     3. It would be confusing to have an empty array `[]` when actually blocking.

On a sidenote, the spec as written is going to have empty arrays when blocking, since the reasons don't currently include all the reasons that browsers currently use.

> As to worker-initiated fetch, Domenic commented that we could add "in the context of document (including any initiated by Workers whose owner set contains the single item document)" here: [#9360 (comment)](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9360#discussion_r1285506518) Let me know if you agree with this or not.

I haven't looked in detail yet, but on first look that makes sense.

>       * unspecced reasons that prevent the page going into BFCache at all (although I would prefer to surface them as specific reasons, not jus bucket them as "internal")

I don't think we should expose reasons like memory pressure, user's preference to turn off BFCache, …

I'm not going to respond on the cross-site issue. We can remove cross-site fromt this PR and land what we agree on, then come back to cross-site later.

> I don't think we should expose reasons like memory pressure, user's preference to turn off BFCache, …

It seems absolutely fine to merge these into "internal". They are not actionable by site authors.

What will it look like when we have a page with

- a.com
   - a.com
      - b.com
'
and .b.com blocks? @petervanderbeken @smaug---- what do you want it to look like?

Somewhat late with this but we are in the process of adding URL and line number information in devtools for each reason. If we were to do that for this API, I don't see a nice way extend it.

Should we make each reason a struct with a name so that later we can add source information?

> What will it look like when we have a page with
> 
>     * a.com
>       
>       * a.com
>         
>         * b.com
>           '
>           and .b.com blocks? @petervanderbeken @smaug---- what do you want it to look like?

@smaug---- and I discussed this, we think that this should be:
```
url: a.com
reasons: [ masked ]
|
+-  url: a.com
    reasons: []
    |
    +- url: b.com
       reasons: []
```

We think the API shouldn't expose information about cross-origin iframes. There is existing information (through the `PageTransitionEvent.persisted` property) that the top page isn't being put in the BFCache, so it seems ok to expose that information on the top page through this API too. I'd even argue that the `masked` special value only makes sense on the top page, it feels like we should not expose things like OOM (or other internal reasons) on a page-specific level.

And it still seems that `preventedBackForwardCache` and the `reasons` array contain redundant information.
Thanks for the feedback, I updated this so that it does not expose cross origin information at all, and instead have "masked" value at the top level. PTAL again.
